hints.title: Check the proposed roots
hints.body: Substitute each reported value into the original equation, using the nonnegative square root.
hints.recap: A squared equation may have roots that fail the original equation.
hints.pitfall: The original equation is the one that decides whether a value works.
hints.pause: Record which reported values really are solutions.

recall.reminder: A squared equation may have roots that fail the original equation.

hints.title: Check each arrow in order
hints.body: At each arrow, ask whether the two equations have exactly the same solutions. Check the allowed inputs as well as the algebra.
hints.recap: An equivalent equation has exactly the same solutions as the original.
hints.pitfall: Correct reported roots do not prove that no others exist.
hints.pause: Look for an allowed input that works before a step but not after it, or the reverse.

recall.reminder: Check whether each algebraic step preserves exactly the same solutions.

solution:
At x=12, the original equation is 0=0, so this is a valid solution. It disappears in step III, which divides by 2x−1 without handling the possibility 2x−1=0.

The other reported values are genuine: x=58 gives both sides 54, and x=52 gives both sides 20. Squaring has therefore not made either listed answer false.

For completeness, the squared equation factors as (2x−1)(8x−5)(2x−5)=0. Checking these three candidates gives the full solution set {12, 58, 52}.

There is another solution, lost at step III: F.
knowledgePattern: Locate a lost solution after division by a zero-capable factor
